assessment.rationale: Partial fit. The envelope cleanly leaves CID verification to payload/CAS layers and avoids central enforcement, but it does not specify the feed-level rejection, retry, or peer-local accounting behavior this corrupt-chunk scenario needs. The unsigned v0 base also weakens accountability under Mallory pressure.
strengths: Clear pcid/payload boundary keeps chunk verification local to the payload protocol instead of introducing central enforcement.
DAG-CBOR canonical bytes and the rule that best-effort output must be marked unsupported and unverified make failure boundaries more auditable.
No central pCID registry assumption fits sparse-knowledge, decentralized operation.
weaknesses: The base envelope has no built-in signature, authorship, or integrity mechanism.
The spec does not define corrupt-chunk rejection records, retry behavior, or peer-local accounting or reputation updates.
Unknown-pCID best-effort salvage is only lightly constrained in adversarial cases.
risks: Mallory can inject bad bytes into an unsigned envelope with no built-in authorship proof.
Best-effort inspection output may be over-trusted by tools or operators even when marked unsupported and unverified.
If payload or feed protocols do not add strict CID checks and local accounting, the scenario remains unsolved.
open_questions: Which payload or feed protocol records local rejection, retry, and peer accounting after a CID mismatch?
Is the unsigned variant strictly [pcid, payload], or are optional signature-related slots still valid as the encoding text implies?
Should best-effort inspection be quarantined or disabled after a hash mismatch?
How will long-term pCID interpretation stay durable once this draft freezes and handler ecosystems evolve?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
